fix(test): a fake launch holds the run, and the daemon test keeps only the wiring (brandon-unfiled-3248.2ywj) (#531)

* fix(test): a held program proves a request does not wait on its run (brandon-unfiled-3248.2ywj)

The test claimed no request waits on a running program, and measured it by a
2 s sleep and daemon-wide `requests.timedOut` holding still. That counter also
moves for any request slow on its own, so the test measured the machine. It was
weaker than its claim too: a render that waited on the run ends at its own wait
budget, before the 200 ms guard, so the old test passes with the rule broken.

The program now runs until the test releases it. A render event that ended
`answered` over the superseded source cannot come from a wait that included the
run, however loaded the machine, so load can delay the proof but not fail it.

The click goes through `click`, which reads a TIMEOUT as the click landing, and
the counts are read past the connection, where the guard is not.

* fix(test): the held program waits at the shared gate, and the proof reads its own render's event (brandon-unfiled-3248.2ywj)

The fixture carried a private copy of `shellGate`'s hold. The proof scanned
the log for any attempt, a timed-out one included, and a failed wait named
only the bar. `renderAnswer` hands back the event of the answer it returned,
so the bytes and the proof are one render, and a failed wait names how that
render ended.

The hold is bounded by the run's own timeout; the comment says so.

* fix(test): a fake launch holds the run, and the daemon test keeps only the wiring (brandon-unfiled-3248.2ywj)

"While the program runs" was proved on a daemon with a real shell, a file
poll, a render poll and log events, so it measured the machine. `Runs` already
takes `launch` as a port, so run-action now holds the run in a fake: no
process, no sleep, no wall-clock bound. The rule that no request waits on a
superseded lane stays where it was pinned, in render-payload-outcomes, over a
lane that never lands.

The daemon test is a wiring check: a click runs the real program through the
storage owner's supersede, and its write draws. `renderAnswer` and the gate are
gone with the hold they served.

* fix(test): a held run is observed across real turns, and a supersede is read by its file (brandon-unfiled-3248.2ywj)

The held test looked at the bar in the click's own tick, so a source resumed
early passed. It now holds through real turns with the program's write on
disk.

The e2e counted supersede refreshes across all of plugin storage, so a
supersede of another session's key passed. It now reads the refresh event of
this session's file, which removes the ledger helper.

Every in-worker stats read goes through statsOf, past the connection's 200 ms
guard, so these files no longer fail on a slow stats reply.

* fix(test): the doctor's stats reads go past the guard, and a fake launch asserts only what it can fail (brandon-unfiled-3248.2ywj)

The doctor e2e's in-worker stats reads move to statsOf, which removes their
casts and the connection's 200 ms guard.

`failed: 0` and the empty click error go back to the real-launch test: a
held launch only resolves ok, so neither could fail there.

The refresh event's expected file is spelled by valueOf, as the daemon logs
it, so a temp path with a space still matches.
